sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: lights, littering, speed zones, braking, stops, railroad and school buses, police stops, yielding, emergency vehicles, buses and turn signals
Confusable pairs and continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and any hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
Never coast downhill in neutral, and in a manual car never coast with the clutch pressed, because both reduce your control. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A01
Tennessee drives on the right, so you go to the right around traffic circles, roundabouts and town squares. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A01
A vehicle stopped or parked on the road or shoulder must show parking lights when visibility is limited, even though driving on parking lights alone is illegal then. [A01]
Why it matters: group lights; confusable parked versus moving.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A01
Since January 1, 2018, steady lights showing to the front of a vehicle must be white or amber, with exceptions for certain vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A02
Also since January 1, 2018, no flashing front-facing lights are allowed other than factory emergency flashers, again with some vehicle exceptions. [A02]
Why it matters: group lights; confusable steady versus flashing front lights.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A02
Any vehicle carrying litter or loose material that could fall or blow onto the highway must keep it enclosed or fully covered by a tarp. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A02
Littering fines run from $50 to $3,000 by amount, plus up to 40 hours of litter pickup and, if the court chooses, up to 8 hours at a recycling center. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A02
On a two-lane road you may not pass a funeral procession, and you may not drive between its vehicles unless an officer directs you to. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A02
Driving below a posted minimum is allowed in bad weather, heavy traffic or on a bad road. [A02]
Why it matters: group slow driving; confusable normal versus poor conditions.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A02
The Basic Speed Rule weighs traffic volume and speed, pedestrians, road surface, width and layout, visibility, weather and your own ability. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A03
If the car ahead stops suddenly and you cannot avoid hitting it, you were breaking the Basic Speed Rule or following too closely, even within the limit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A03
The manual says slow drivers are as likely to crash as speeders, so keep pace with traffic that is moving within the limit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A03
If the interstate minimum speed is too fast for you, take another road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A03
The state, counties and cities each set speed limits on their own roads, and some residential streets are limited to 25 or 35 mph at all times. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A03
School zone limits apply while children are going to or from school and during recess. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A03
Work zones include utility work, tree trimming and surveying, and are marked by orange or yellow-green signs, flashing equipment lights and brightly dressed workers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-R17 | anchor: A03
The manual reports that Tennessee work zone crashes in 2021 killed 26 people, injured 1,105 and caused 3,010 property damage cases. [A03]
Why it matters: group work zones; dated figure.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-R18 | anchor: A04
By law every car needs two separate ways of applying the brakes, usually the foot brake and a parking or emergency brake. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec08-R19 | anchor: A04
In a manual car you can slow for a stop by first flashing your brake lights to warn drivers behind, then shifting to a lower gear. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec08-R20 | anchor: A04
Noise and vibration in the pedal are normal when anti-lock brakes work, and lifting off or pumping the pedal disengages them. [A04]
Why it matters: group brakes; confusable ABS versus non-ABS skid response.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec08-R21 | anchor: A04
Riding the brake wears out the brakes and falsely tells drivers behind that you are about to stop. [A04]
Why it matters: group brakes; confusable covering versus riding.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec08-R22 | anchor: A04
Tennessee law forbids following another vehicle more closely than is reasonable for the speed, traffic and road conditions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec08-R23 | anchor: A05
If the two-second count shows you are too close, ease off and recheck at another fixed point until you are at least two seconds back. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec08-R24 | anchor: A05
Stopping distance depends on the pavement, tires, brakes, shock absorbers and the vehicle's weight when loaded or towing. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec08-R25 | anchor: A05
The manual cites the National Safety Council: a light passenger car at 50 mph can stop in about 200 feet. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec08-R26 | anchor: A06
If you cannot see cross traffic after stopping, edge forward slowly until you can see both ways, and wait for anyone in the crosswalk to finish crossing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec08-R27 | anchor: A06
After the car ahead clears the intersection, pull up to the stop line and come to a full stop again yourself. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec08-R28 | anchor: A06
Officers and instructors say a car has fully stopped only when you feel it lurch forward after all motion ends. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec08-R29 | anchor: A06
You must stop completely when a flagger at a construction site or a police officer signals you to stop. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec08-R30 | anchor: A06
Railroad crossing pavement markings include a large X, the letters RR, a no-passing stripe and a stop line, and breaking railroad signals carries the same penalties as other traffic devices. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec08-R31 | anchor: A07
A bus about to stop at a railroad crossing pulls right with its stoplights on, and tankers required to stop usually turn on emergency flashers. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec08-R32 | anchor: A07
Never pass a stopped school bus on the right, where children get on and off; stay stopped until it moves, its driver waves you on or its signals go off. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec08-R33 | anchor: A07
When a school bus stops at an intersection to load or unload children, drivers coming from every direction must stop. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec08-R34 | anchor: A08
When a police car signals you with flashing blue or blue and red lights or a siren, pull over close to the right edge, clear of any intersection, and stop. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-R35 | anchor: A08
During a traffic stop keep your hands on the wheel, keep passengers' hands visible, tell the officer if you hold a handgun permit and are armed, stay inside, and switch on the interior light after dark. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-R36 | anchor: A08
Do not argue with an officer at the scene, since violations are decided in court, and if an unmarked car signals you, you may drive slowly to a nearby populated spot before stopping. [A08]
Why it matters: group police stops; confusable marked versus unmarked car.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-R37 | anchor: A09
Yield to pedestrians crossing with the light when you turn a corner and when you cross a sidewalk from a driveway, alley or lot; driving on a sidewalk is illegal except to cross it. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-R38 | anchor: A09
Drive with extreme caution where children may be playing, and slow down near schools, playgrounds and residential areas. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-R39 | anchor: A09
Yield to traffic already in a roundabout, to moving traffic when leaving a parked position, to highway traffic when merging, and to an emergency vehicle backing into a fire station. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-R40 | anchor: A10
Yield to any vehicle already in the intersection even on your green, and on the dead-end road of a T intersection yield to traffic both ways on the main road. [A10]
Why it matters: group yielding; confusable green light versus vehicle already in intersection.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-R41 | anchor: A10
Private vehicles may not carry or show blue, or blue and red, flashing emergency lights unless authorized. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-R42 | anchor: A10
Never follow a fire truck answering an alarm, never drive within the block where it has stopped, and never run over a fire hose without permission from the officer in charge. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-R43 | anchor: A10
For an emergency vehicle, clear the intersection before pulling over, avoid blocking a side road, and at a red light stay put even if it turns green before the vehicle passes. [A10]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; confusable pull over versus clear the intersection.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-R44 | anchor: A10
Yield to a metro transit bus that has signaled and is pulling back into traffic from a bus stop. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-R45 | anchor: A11
Unlike a school bus, a transit bus stopped for passengers does not require you to stop and may be passed, but watch for riders crossing. [A11]
Why it matters: group buses; confusable school bus versus transit bus.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-R46 | anchor: A11
The Move Over requirement applies only on roads with two or more lanes in your direction when the stopped vehicle is on your side of the road. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-R47 | anchor: A11
The most common turning faults are not signaling, signaling too briefly, not searching for hazards, turning from the wrong lane and turning improperly. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-R48 | anchor: A11
Turn from the lane closest to your direction of turn into the closest legal lane, and remember that signaling never gives you the right-of-way. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-R49 | anchor: A11
Hand signals help in bright sun or heavy traffic but are hard to see at night, and you should pull your arm in to steer during the turn. [A11]
Why it matters: group turning; confusable hand signals versus signal lights.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-R50 | anchor: A11
Tap the brakes a few times to flash your brake lights before stopping, and cancel your turn signal afterward so it does not mislead others. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0069]
